Title: Drivers of woody dominance across global drylands
Approach: Compared relative abundance of shrubs between coarse- and fine-textured soils across a precipitation gradient.
ITE Results: Shrub dominance occurred on fine-textured soils below ~380 mm MAP and on coarse-textured soils above this point, suggesting the opposite of the ITE.

Author: Biancari, Lucio; Aguiar, Martin; Saiz, Hugo; Gross, Nicolas; Le Bagousse-Pinguet, Yoann; Eldridge, David; Maestre, Fernando
Title: Upper boundary on tree cover at global drylands
Approach: Compared maximum tree cover between coarse- and fine-textured soils along a precipitation gradient.
ITE Results: ITE not evident for maximum tree cover--and coarse soils have higher maximum tree cover at both low and high precipitation (~30-900 mm MAP).

Title: Analytical model for bare soil evaporation dynamics following wetting with concurrent internal drainage
Approach: Compared soil water balance consequences of evaporation with concurrent drainage across soil texturs.
ITE Results: Provide mechanism and analytical model supporting ITE in arid regions whereby rapid drying of surface layers in coarse soils allows water to percolate rapidly to depths where it is protected from evaporation and available to plants. Greatest evaporative losses occur with small events on loamy soils.

Author: Lomax, Guy A.; Powell, Thomas WR; Lenton, Timothy M.; Economou, Theo; Cunliffe, Andrew M.
Title: Untangling the environmental drivers of gross primary productivity in African rangelands
Approach: Compared gross primary productivity across vegetation types and precipitation, temperature, and nitrogen gradients.
ITE Results: Sand increased productivity across the precipitation gradient (~100-1500 mm MAP) for all vegetation types (grassland, shrubland, savanna).

Author: Suliman, Mahmoud; Scaini, Anna; Manzoni, Stefano; Vico, Giulia
Title: Soil properties modulate actual evapotranspiration and precipitation impacts on crop yields in the USA
Approach: Compared crop yields across climate and soil gradients.
ITE Results: Maximum yeild of crops on coarse-textured soils occurred at lower precipitation values than on fine-textured soils. Crop yields were higher on coarse-textured soils under dry conditions and lower under wetter conditions.

Author: Terry, Tyson J.; Adler, Peter B.
Title: Precipitation seasonality and soil texture interact to shape dryland recovery from severe disturbance
Approach: Compared net primary productivity between disturbed and undisturbed habitat across precipitation and soil texture gradients.
ITE Results: Recovery of shrubs lower on coarse- than fine-textured soils and at warm sites, perhaps due to recruitment failure when shallow surface layers dry out quickly.
